page.layout: One page of running text in a single column, with narrow margins on both sides. Running head centred at the top. Page number at the top. No notes in the margins. Edge fragments at both margins are not printed text.

main_text.p: mediterraneum ab occasu in ortum porrectæ, quæ Numidiam in orientem sequitur, & proprie Africa, sive Africa minor, ac regio Carthaginiensis nuncupatur, incredibilis fertilitatis, & cœli serenissimi, duo promontoria in mare se efferunt ex adverso maris Tyrrheni & Italiæ, quorum alterum, quod occidentem spectat, Apollinis, alterum quod orientem, Mercurii veteres appellarunt. Inter quæ promontoria sinus est medius modicè in meridiem descedens ac se curvans. In hoc sinu duæ nobiles urbes quondam floruere VTICA & CARTHAGO, non admodum longo intervallo inter se distantes, utraque à Phœnicibus orta. Sed Vtica multo no-[illegible, ~3 letters]ior & major & potentior fuit Carthago, cujus rempublicam descripsimus. De hac Polybius historiographus, qui ipsam incolumem florentemque vidit, & in obsidione atque excidio ejusdem cum P. Scipione Æmiliano Rom. imperatore fuit, sic scribit libro primo, exponens bellum, quod Afri cum cæteris mercenariis statim post finitum bellum Punicum primum inter æmulas civitates Carthaginem & Romam summâ animorum pertinaciâ per annos xxiii gestum, Carthaginiensibus intulêre: Vrbs namq; hæc Carthago in sinum quen-

page.notes: Printed "ortum" is followed by a flourish or arrow-like mark at the line end, not a hyphen; left as "ortum". The word after "no-" at the line break is partly hidden by a stain at the left edge; the middle letters are illegible. Fragments at the left edge (small o, i, and marks) and at the right edge (small marks, possibly show-through or the neighbouring page) are not transcribed. A faint mark under the last line is not a catchword or signature.
